Bail Bond Information for Maricopa County

After booking into Maricopa County jail, a judge typically sets bail at arraignment (often within 24–72 hours). Families often work with a licensed bail bondsman. A common commercial bond fee is about 10% of the bail amount (non-refundable). Example: $10,000 bail → roughly $1,000 premium, subject to local rules.

If the person cannot afford bail, they may request a reduction hearing or public defender.

For hearing schedules, contact the Maricopa County court.

Visitation Rules at Maricopa County Jail

Policies vary. Before visiting Maricopa County Jail, confirm:

  • Approved ID: Government-issued photo ID
  • Hours: Call Maricopa County Sheriff's Office for the current schedule
  • Dress code: Facilities restrict clothing that resembles uniforms
  • Video visits: Many jails offer remote options — ask when you call
  • Children: Minors usually need an accompanying adult

What to Expect After Arrest in Maricopa County

Typical steps after arrest in Maricopa County:

  1. Booking — fingerprints, photo, property inventory
  2. Medical screening — before general population housing
  3. Classification — housing based on charges and history
  4. Arraignment — first court appearance; bail often set here
  5. Transfer — serious cases may move to a state facility

Frequently Asked Questions — Maricopa County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Maricopa County jail?

Start with the official Maricopa County inmate roster. You can also call Maricopa County Sheriff's Office at (602) 876-0322. Online records often lag booking by a few hours.

What is the phone number for Maricopa County Jail?

Contact Maricopa County Sheriff's Office at (602) 876-0322. Facility address on file: 550 W Jackson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003.

How long does booking take in Maricopa County?

Booking commonly takes 2–8 hours depending on volume at Maricopa County Jail. Weekends and holidays can delay when a name appears in any published system. If urgent, call the facility directly rather than waiting on a website refresh.

Can I visit an inmate at Maricopa County jail?

Usually yes if the person is eligible and the facility is accepting visits. The main facility listed is Maricopa County Jail at 550 W Jackson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003. Bring government photo ID and confirm hours and dress code with Maricopa County Sheriff's Office before you go. Video visitation may be offered.

What if the person is not listed in the county system?

They may have been released, transferred, or booked under a different name spelling. Check Arizona Department of Corrections and the Federal BOP locator for federal custody. Then call Maricopa County Sheriff's Office to confirm.

How do I send money to someone at Maricopa County Jail?

Ask Maricopa County Jail which commissary vendor they use (often JPay, Securus, or Access Corrections) when you call (602) 876-0322. Limits and fees vary by facility — confirm before sending money.
